public_rationale: For the latest reported quarter, Microsoft described Azure AI as capacity constrained and attributed stronger results to earlier capacity delivery. That contradicts the broad claim that it had already built more usable capacity than customers demanded. Lease cancellations support concern about future requirements, but do not establish that current demand was below installed capacity.
limitations: The decisive evidence is Microsoft's own operating account, not independent utilization measurement.
The result applies to overall Azure AI customer demand, not every facility or household demand alone.
The February cancellation reports concern a later period than the selected reported quarter.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft appears to have built too much capacity relative to actual consumer demand.

statement.excerpt: Sounds like Microsoft built too much capacity, and in fact has yet to see the consumer demand to actually reach it!

from_speaker: has yet to see the consumer demand to actually reach it
our_interpretation: Read the claim as an existing overall surplus of usable Azure AI capacity relative to customer demand.
In context, consumer demand refers to customers consuming Microsoft's services, including business customers; it is not limited to household purchases.
Use Microsoft's fiscal second quarter, October through December 2024, as the latest completed publicly reported quarter before the post.
Distinguish existing usable capacity from prospective leases and future construction.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence for the target quarter shows that usable Azure AI capacity exceeded customer demand overall, leaving a material surplus.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence for the target quarter shows that customer demand remained constrained by available Azure AI capacity.
